title: 'Working at Google from 2007-09 to 2026-10 gave me a first-row seat to see it gradually become corrupted'
summary: A Goodreads reviewer who spent nineteen years at Google says the span let him watch the place take more and more short-term decisions. His review sets out four contributions chapter by chapter: organizations as systems stronger than any individual, financial gravity made explicit, profit redefined as the maximization of human flourishing, and steward ownership widened into what the book calls Spiritual Holding Companies. He also notes the spread of examples, from Patagonia and Novo Nordisk to Mondragon and Costco.
blockquote: I had been thinking about this topic for a long time. Working at Google from 2007-09 to 2026-10 gave me a first-row seat to see it gradually become corrupted —for example, start taking more and more questionable decisions based on short-term gains. The ideas in this book resonated strongly with me.
attribution_title: Goodreads reviewer · nineteen years at Google (2007–2026)
